overlays.title: Servicemembers Civil Relief Act — Covered Residential Eviction
overlays.rule: For covered premises and statutory conditions, eviction during military service generally requires a court order; qualifying material-effect cases can support a stay or adjustment.
overlays.warning: SCRA coverage depends on covered military-service status and statutory conditions. Veteran status alone does not create this protection.

overlays.title: Servicemembers Civil Relief Act — Mortgage / Trust-Deed Protection
overlays.rule: Section 3953 applies to a qualifying mortgage, trust deed, or similar security obligation that originated before the servicemember's military service and remains the servicemember's obligation. Covered sale, foreclosure, or seizure during military service or within one year afterward is generally invalid without a qualifying court order or statutory agreement; courts also have stay/adjustment authority when military service materially affects compliance.
overlays.warning: This protection is timing- and service-status-specific. It is not a general veteran foreclosure protection.

overlays.title: Servicemembers Civil Relief Act — Default Judgment Protections
overlays.rule: Before certain default judgments, courts require military-status information and the statute provides attorney/stay protections in specified circumstances.
overlays.warning: This is not a substitute for appearing in court when possible.

overlays.title: Regulation X — Early Intervention
overlays.rule: Subject to Regulation X scope and exceptions, servicers must make good-faith efforts to establish live contact with a delinquent borrower no later than the 36th day of delinquency and provide required written early-intervention information by the applicable rule schedule.
overlays.warning: Regulation X has scope provisions, exemptions, and fact-specific servicing rules; do not assume every mortgage or servicer is covered identically.

overlays.title: Regulation X — Continuity of Contact
overlays.rule: Covered servicers must maintain policies reasonably designed to assign personnel to delinquent borrowers and provide information about available loss mitigation, application status, foreclosure referral circumstances, and applicable deadlines.
overlays.warning: This is a servicing-process protection, not a promise that a particular modification will be offered.

overlays.title: Regulation X — Loss Mitigation / Foreclosure Restrictions
overlays.rule: For covered mortgage servicing, §1024.41 regulates handling of loss-mitigation applications and restricts certain foreclosure steps in specified circumstances. It expressly does not require a servicer to offer any particular loss-mitigation option.
overlays.warning: Coverage, timing, completeness of the application, prior applications, delinquency stage, and statutory exceptions matter. Do not reduce the rule to a generic 'dual tracking is illegal' statement.

overlays.title: Fair Housing Act — Disability Reasonable Accommodation
overlays.rule: Disability discrimination can include refusing a reasonable accommodation in rules, policies, practices, or services when the accommodation may be necessary for equal use and enjoyment of a dwelling.
overlays.warning: Accommodation is not an automatic eviction defense. Necessity, nexus, reasonableness, undue burden, fundamental alteration, timing, and statutory coverage can matter.

overlays.title: HUD Public Housing — Program-Specific Termination / Grievance Overlay
overlays.authority: HUD public-housing regulations and current PHA procedures
overlays.rule: Public-housing residents may have program-specific notice and grievance procedures in addition to state eviction procedure. The exact route depends on the termination ground and governing PHA documents/regulations.
overlays.warning: Do not apply private-market notice assumptions or assume every public-housing termination receives the same grievance path.

overlays.title: Housing Choice Voucher — Assistance / Tenancy Overlay
overlays.authority: HUD Housing Choice Voucher program rules
overlays.rule: Voucher tenancy and PHA assistance decisions can create program-specific notice or review rights separate from the landlord's state-court eviction case.
overlays.warning: Owner termination, PHA termination of assistance, and state-court eviction are different decisions and must not be collapsed into one appeal.

overlays.title: HUD-VASH
overlays.rule: HUD-VASH combines Housing Choice Voucher rental assistance with VA case management/supportive services for eligible Veterans experiencing homelessness.
overlays.warning: HUD-VASH is not itself an eviction defense, and voucher availability, local administration, eligibility, and placement are not guaranteed.

overlays.title: Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF)
overlays.rule: SSVF grantees provide homelessness-prevention and rapid-rehousing assistance to eligible very-low-income Veteran families through local providers.
overlays.warning: SSVF is not a statutory entitlement; services, funding, eligibility determinations, and local availability vary.

overlays.title: Legal Services for Veterans — Homeless Veterans and Veterans At-Risk for Homelessness (LSV-H)
overlays.rule: VA funds legal services for eligible Veterans who are homeless or at risk through grantees whose work can include housing-related civil legal matters.
overlays.warning: LSV-H does not guarantee representation, and not every grantee provides every listed service.

overlays.title: VA Home Loan Foreclosure-Avoidance Assistance
overlays.rule: VA-backed loans are generally private loans backed by a VA guaranty. Borrowers should work with the servicer and may contact a VA loan technician. VA currently lists foreclosure-avoidance options including special forbearance, repayment plans, modifications, and the VA Partial Claim Program where eligible.
overlays.warning: VA does not automatically own or directly service a VA-backed mortgage. Availability and eligibility for a particular loss-mitigation option are case-specific.

overlays.title: HUD Project-Based Section 8 / Multifamily Assistance — Program-Specific Termination Overlay
overlays.authority: HUD Handbook 4350.3, Chapter 8 / applicable multifamily program regulations
overlays.rule: Project-based Section 8 and related HUD multifamily assistance can create program-specific lease-termination, subsidy/assistance, written-notice, and judicial-eviction requirements that are separate from public housing, Housing Choice Voucher administration, HUD-VASH, and California unlawful-detainer procedure.
overlays.warning: Identify the exact multifamily program and governing project documents before applying a termination rule. Loss of subsidy, lease termination, owner termination, and state-court eviction are distinct events. No program-specific deadline is published in this overlay.

steps: Identify the housing rule, lease term, policy, service, or procedure creating the disability-related problem.
Identify the disability-related need and the connection between the requested change and equal use or enjoyment of the housing.
Request the specific reasonable accommodation. Written requests are useful for proof, though the legal analysis does not depend on magic wording.

If disability or need is not apparent, provide only reliable disability-related information reasonably necessary to verify disability and nexus. Full medical records and detailed diagnosis are generally unnecessary for this inquiry.
Preserve the request, supporting information, delivery proof, landlord/PHA response, and any proposed alternative accommodation.
If denied or ignored and housing is at risk, contact legal aid and consider a HUD/FHEO complaint promptly.
limits: A provider may evaluate necessity and reasonableness and may raise undue financial/administrative burden or fundamental-alteration limits where legally applicable.
Do not advise a tenant to volunteer complete medical files merely to request an accommodation.

hud_complaint.deadline_summary: HUD states Fair Housing Act allegations generally must be filed within one year of the last alleged discriminatory act; other judicial limitation periods can differ.
